source: Order from the 2018 Turkish word list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave (CC BY-SA 4.0), built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus (opensubtitles.org, via OPUS; Lison, Tiedemann and Kouylekov 2018), so it reflects film and TV dialogue. Forms were lowercased and merged into lemmas with the zeyrek analyser (a Python port of Zemberek-NLP), forms that fit two lemmas were split in proportion to how common each lemma is, and the result was cleaned by hand: names, fragments and obscenities removed, some words turned into phrase or compound-verb cards. Ranks are estimates, not exact corpus counts. The ranked list is scripts/turkish/wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkish/PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

ex.en: Your Turkish has really improved!

cards.note: From *ileri* (forward). The e becomes i before `-(I)yor`: *ilerliyor*. *İlerleme* = progress.

ex.en: The child jumped into the pool.

cards.note: Where you jump takes the dative: *suya atlamak*. Also to skip: *Bu soruyu atla* (Skip this question). The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *atlıyor*.

ex.en: My new shoes are a bit tight.

cards.note: *Ayak* (foot) + *kap* (container). *Ayakkabı numaran kaç?* = What's your shoe size? In Turkish homes, shoes usually come off at the door.

ex.en: We met at a bar in the evening.

cards.note: A loanword, as in English. A café is *kafe*; a traditional tavern serving rakı and meze is a *meyhane*.

ex.en: Congratulations on your new job!

cards.note: *Tebrik ederim* is a little more formal. *Tebrikler* can be said to anyone; *Aferin* (well done) is said to a child or someone younger.

ex.en: Have you thought about every possible outcome?

cards.note: A little formal; in speech *mümkün* or *muhtemel* are more common. *Olasılık* = probability, possibility.

ex.tr: Bu ilacın etkisi ne zaman başlar?
ex.en: When does this medicine start working?

cards.note: *Etkilemek* = to affect, to impress; *etkili* = effective. The effect of X on Y: *X'in Y üzerindeki etkisi*.

ex.en: Which outfit are you going to wear to the wedding?

cards.note: One *kıyafet* can be a whole outfit; *kıyafetler* = clothes. Synonyms: *giysi*, and *elbise* (also a dress).

ex.tr: Kapının önünde şüpheli bir adam var.
ex.en: There's a suspicious man in front of the door.

cards.note: From *şüphe* (doubt, suspicion). As a noun, the suspect in a crime: *Şüpheli kaçtı* (The suspect escaped).

ex.tr: Bir kâğıt ve kalem verir misin?
ex.en: Could you give me a piece of paper and a pen?

cards.note: Spelled with â (TDK). The t becomes d before a vowel: *kâğıdı*. *Kâğıt oynamak* = to play cards.

en: to lower, to put down, to take down

ex.en: Could you drop me off at the corner?

cards.note: Causative of *inmek* (to go down, to get off). *Silahını indir!* = Put the gun down! *İndirim* = discount.

ex.en: There are eight planets in the solar system.

cards.note: From *gezmek* (to wander), like the Greek word behind **planet**. *Dünya* = the Earth; the world.

ex.en: The bank closes at five.

cards.note: *Banka hesabı* = bank account; *bankamatik* or *ATM* = cash machine.

ex.en: Don't give up on your dreams!

cards.note: What you give up takes the ablative: *bu fikirden vazgeçmek*. Alone, to change your mind: *Vazgeçtim, gelmiyorum* (I changed my mind, I'm not coming).

ex.en: This bread is very hard.

cards.note: Opposite of *yumuşak* (soft). Of people, strict or harsh: *sert bir öğretmen*; of coffee or wind, strong: *sert bir rüzgâr*.

ex.en: How much do I owe you?

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *borcu*. *Borç vermek* = to lend; *borç almak* = to borrow; *Borcum ne kadar?* = How much do I owe? (in a shop).

ex.en: Dear passengers, our plane is landing in Istanbul.

cards.note: Formal, before a surname, a full name or a title, in letters and announcements: *Sayın Ayşe Demir*, *Sayın Yetkili* (To whom it may concern). In everyday speech, *Bey* and *Hanım* follow the first name instead.

ex.en: Smoking is not allowed here.

cards.note: *Sigara içmek* = to smoke, literally to drink a cigarette. *Sigarayı bıraktım* = I quit smoking.

ex.tr: Bu valiz çok ağır, yardım eder misin?
ex.en: This suitcase is very heavy; can you help?

cards.note: Opposite of *hafif* (light). Also serious, *ağır yaralı* (seriously injured), and slow, *ağır ağır* (slowly).

ex.en: Most of my friends live in Istanbul.

cards.note: *Çok* + the possessive: *arkadaşlarımın çoğu* (most of my friends), *çoğumuz* (most of us). Before a noun: *çoğu insan* (most people). *Çoğu zaman* = most of the time.

ex.tr: Ciddi bir hastalık değil, merak etme.
ex.en: It's not a serious illness; don't worry.

cards.note: *Hasta* (ill) + `-lIk`; the k becomes ğ before a vowel: *hastalığı*. *Hastalanmak* = to fall ill.

ex.en: Excuse me, where's the washroom?

cards.note: In a restaurant also *lavabo* (more discreet) or *WC*; at home, the bathroom is *banyo*. *Tuvalet kâğıdı* = toilet paper.

en: to be quiet, to stop talking

ex.en: Quiet, the baby's sleeping!

cards.note: *Sus!* = Be quiet! (blunt); politer: *Lütfen sessiz olun*. Not to be confused with *susamak* (to get thirsty).

ex.en: This smell is disgusting!

cards.note: Strong and colloquial. From *iğrenmek* (to be disgusted, by: ablative). Milder: *Hiç güzel değil*.

ex.en: This soup tastes really good.

cards.note: One of the few one-syllable words whose t becomes d before a vowel: *tadı*. *Tadına bakmak* = to taste; *tatlı* = sweet.

en: because of, due to (after the ablative)

ex.en: Schools are closed because of the snow.

cards.note: Follows the ablative: *yağmurdan dolayı*. Close to *yüzünden* (often for something bad) and *nedeniyle* (formal). *Dolayısıyla* = consequently.

ex.en: May I see your ID?

cards.note: *Kim* (who) + `-lIk`; the k becomes ğ before a vowel: *kimliği*. *Kimlik kartı*, or just *kimlik* = ID card.

en: shore, bank (of the sea, a river)

ex.en: They have a house by the sea.

cards.note: Used like a place noun: *masanın kenarında* (on the edge of the table). *Deniz kenarı* = seaside; *yol kenarı* = roadside; *kenara çekmek* = to pull over.

ex.en: It's a pleasure working with you.

cards.note: *Zevk almak* = to enjoy, with the ablative: *müzikten zevk almak*. *Zevkine göre* = to your taste; *zevkli* = tasteful.

ex.en: If we stand together, we'll win.

cards.note: *Bir* + `-lIk`; the k becomes ğ before a vowel: *birliği*. *Birlik olmak* = to unite; *Avrupa Birliği* = the European Union. Not *birlikte* (together).

ex.en: I don't like horror movies at all.

cards.note: From *korkmak* (to be afraid). *Korku filmi* = horror movie; *korkunç* = terrible, awful.

ex.en: There used to be a movie theatre here.

cards.note: *Eski* (old) + the ablative. Often with `-(I)rdI` for past habits: *Eskiden çok kitap okurdum* (I used to read a lot).

ex.en: You were very drunk last night.

cards.note: *Sarhoş olmak* = to get drunk. Also figurative: *mutluluktan sarhoş* (drunk with happiness).

ex.en: I'll hand in my homework tomorrow.

cards.note: To whom: dative, *paketi müşteriye teslim etmek*. *Teslim olmak* = to surrender, to give yourself up: *Polise teslim oldu*.

ex.en: We wandered around the city all day.

cards.note: Where takes the locative (*parkta dolaşmak*) or the accusative (*dünyayı dolaşmak*, to travel around the world). *Dolaşmaya çıkmak* = to go for a walk.

ex.tr: Bu kadar işi bir günde bitirmek imkânsız.
ex.en: It's impossible to finish this much work in one day.

cards.note: Spelled with â (TDK): *imkân* (possibility) + `-sIz`. Synonym: *olanaksız*; opposite: *mümkün*.

ex.en: My dad is my hero.

cards.note: Also the main character of a novel or a film. *Kahramanlık* = heroism; *halk kahramanı* = folk hero.

ex.en: Is that a threat?

cards.note: The t becomes d before a vowel: *tehdidi*. *Tehdit etmek* = to threaten: *Beni tehdit mi ediyorsun?*

ex.en: Who beat him up?

cards.note: To hit someone again and again. *Dövüşmek* = to fight each other; *dövme* = tattoo.

en: to burn, to be on fire

ex.en: Something's burning in the kitchen!

cards.note: Intransitive; to burn something is *yakmak*. Of a light: *Işık yanıyor* (The light is on). *Güneşte yandım* = I got sunburned.

ex.en: Where's my black bag?

cards.note: Like the other colour words, a noun and an adjective. *Siyah* is the everyday colour word; *kara* is mostly figurative or in set phrases (*Karadeniz*).

ex.en: Nonsense! Nobody will believe that.

cards.note: Often an adjective: *Bu çok saçma* (That's ridiculous). *Saçmalamak* = to talk nonsense: *Saçmalama!* *Saçma sapan* = nonsensical.

ex.en: I don't eat meat; I'm vegetarian.

cards.note: *Kırmızı et* = red meat; *dana eti* = beef; *tavuk eti* = chicken. Not the imperative *et* of *etmek*.

ex.en: That doesn't matter at all.

cards.note: *Önemli* = important; *önem vermek* = to care about, to value (dative); *Önemi yok* = It doesn't matter.

en: to be kept, to be stored

ex.en: The cat hid under the bed again.

cards.note: Reflexive of *saklamak* (to hide something, to keep). Where takes the dative (*dolaba saklanmak*) or the locative (*dolapta saklanmak*). *Saklambaç* = hide-and-seek.

ex.tr: Ali ile Can çok sıkı arkadaş.
ex.en: Ali and Can are very close friends.

cards.note: *Sıkı çalışmak* = to work hard; *Sıkı tutun!* = Hold on tight! *Sıkı fıkı* = very close, thick as thieves. Not *sık* (often).

ex.en: I'm a member of this club.

cards.note: *Üye olmak* = to become a member, to join (dative: *kulübe üye olmak*). *Üyelik* = membership.

ex.en: The service at this hotel is very good.

cards.note: *Hizmet etmek* = to serve (dative). *Hizmetinizdeyim* = At your service.

ex.en: I made an appointment with the doctor.

cards.note: *Randevu almak* = to make an appointment, from someone: ablative. A date with someone is also *randevu*, or colloquially *buluşma*.

ex.en: She's the daughter of a very rich family.

cards.note: Opposite of *fakir* or *yoksul* (poor). As a noun, a rich person: *zenginler*. *Zenginlik* = wealth.

ex.en: There's a little cat in the garden.

cards.note: Istanbul is known for its street cats, fed by whole neighbourhoods. A kitten is *yavru kedi*.

ex.en: We have no other choice.

cards.note: From *seçmek* (to choose); the k becomes ğ before a vowel: *seçeneği*. Synonym: *alternatif*.

ex.en: The shop on the corner is open on Sunday.

cards.note: Spelled with â (TDK). Usually a small shop; a big store is a *mağaza*. *Dükkâncı* = shopkeeper.

ex.en: What's the English equivalent of this word?

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *karşılığı*. *Karşılık vermek* = to answer back; *karşılığında* = in return for: *Yardımı karşılığında para istemedi*.

ex.en: I don't want to take this risk.

cards.note: *Risk almak* = to take a risk; *riskli* = risky.

ex.tr: Yatağın altında canavar yok, uyu artık.
ex.en: There's no monster under the bed; go to sleep now.

cards.note: Also said of a cruel person: *O adam bir canavar!*

ex.en: My patience has its limits too!

cards.note: *Sınır kapısı* = border crossing; *sınırlı* = limited; *sınırsız* = unlimited.

en: a friendly way to address a man a little older than you

ex.tr: Abi, bu otobüs Kadıköy'e gidiyor mu?
ex.en: Excuse me, does this bus go to Kadıköy?

cards.note: The spoken form of *ağabey*. To a brother, or as friendly address to a man a bit older: *Ali abi* (lowercase after a name). The female counterpart is *abla*.

ex.en: My grandmother prays every evening.

cards.note: *Dua etmek* = to pray; *senin için dua edeceğim* = I'll pray for you. Also said of good wishes for someone.

ex.en: Did you buy flowers for your mom?

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *çiçeği*. *Çiçek açmak* = to bloom; *çiçekçi* = florist.

ex.tr: Bu çılgın bir fikir, ama hoşuma gitti.
ex.en: That's a crazy idea, but I like it.

cards.note: Often admiring: *çılgın bir parti* (a wild party). *Çılgınlık* = madness. The everyday word for mad is *deli*.

ex.en: You really scared me!

cards.note: Causative of *korkmak* (to be afraid). The person scared takes the accusative: *çocukları korkutma*.

ex.en: I felt like an idiot.

cards.note: Colloquial, and rude when said to someone: *Salak!* Close to *aptal*. The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *Ne kadar salağım!* (How stupid of me!).

ex.tr: Bu toprak domates için çok iyi.
ex.en: This soil is very good for tomatoes.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *toprağı*. The plural *topraklar* often means lands, territory.

ex.tr: Geçen ay yeni bir eve taşındık.
ex.en: We moved to a new house last month.

cards.note: Passive or reflexive of *taşımak* (to carry). Where you move to takes the dative: *İzmir'e taşınmak*.

ex.en: We went hiking in the forest on the weekend.

cards.note: *Orman yangını* = forest fire; *ormanlık* = wooded.

en: to move away, to go away

ex.en: Please move away from the door.

cards.note: From *uzak* (far) + `-lAş`. What you move away from takes the ablative. Also of people: *Zamanla uzaklaştık* (We drifted apart over time).

ex.en: This isn't my style.

cards.note: *Giyim tarzı* = style of dress; *bu tarz şeyler* = things like this.

ex.en: Children need love and patience.

cards.note: From *sevmek*. Calmer and broader than *aşk* (romantic love): love for family, friends, animals. *Sevgiler* closes a friendly message (Love, …).

en: to feel sorry for, to pity (dative)

ex.en: My foot really hurts.

cards.note: What hurts is the subject: *Dizim acıyor* (My knee hurts); for aches, *ağrımak*. With the dative, to pity: *Ona acıyorum*. Not *acıkmak* (to get hungry).

ex.en: Do you come here often?

cards.note: Usually doubled: *sık sık* = often. As an adjective, dense or close together: *sık bir orman*. Not *sıkı* (tight, strict).

en: to be wrong, to be mistaken

ex.en: I think I was wrong; I'm sorry.

cards.note: Of a person's judgment: *Yanılıyorsun* (You're wrong). *Yanılmıyorsam* = If I'm not mistaken. A wrong answer is *yanlış*.

ex.en: I bought some nasal spray at the pharmacy.

cards.note: The u drops before a vowel: *burnu*, *burnum*. *Burnum akıyor* = My nose is running; *burun kıvırmak* = to turn up your nose.

ex.en: Please don't shout at me!

cards.note: Who you shout at takes the dative: *çocuklara bağırmak*. *Bağırış* = a shout, shouting.

ex.en: My son plays for a soccer club.

cards.note: The p becomes b before a vowel: *kulübü*. *Futbol kulübü* = soccer club; *gece kulübü* = nightclub.

en: to get lost, to clear off (rude)

ex.tr: Defol, seni bir daha görmek istemiyorum!
ex.en: Get lost, I don't want to see you again!

cards.note: Rude, mostly in the imperative: *Defol!*, *Defolun!*, *Defol git!* Frequent in dubbed films; best avoided in real life.

ex.en: Is this ring real gold?

cards.note: Also an adjective: *altın yüzük* (gold ring). Small gold coins (*çeyrek altın*) are a traditional wedding present.

ex.tr: Bir itirafım var: pastayı ben yedim.
ex.en: I have a confession: I ate the cake.

cards.note: *İtiraf etmek* = to confess, to admit: *Suçunu itiraf etti*. *İtiraf etmeliyim ki…* = I must admit that…

ex.en: My dad is having surgery tomorrow.

cards.note: *Ameliyat olmak* = to have an operation; *ameliyat etmek* = to operate on someone.

ex.en: Do you want sugar in your tea?

cards.note: *Şekerli* = with sugar; *şekersiz* = without. Colloquially also diabetes: *Babamda şeker var*. *Şeker Bayramı* = the holiday at the end of Ramadan.

ex.tr: Köyün ortasında eski bir kilise var.
ex.en: There's an old church in the middle of the village.

cards.note: A mosque is a *cami* (*camii* with the possessive); a synagogue is a *sinagog* (also *havra*).

ex.en: What's your opinion on this?

cards.note: From *düşünmek*. Not *düşününce* (when you think). *Düşünceli* = thoughtful; also worried.

ex.en: I don't watch TV in the evenings.

cards.note: *Televizyon izlemek* (or *seyretmek*) = to watch TV; *televizyonda* = on TV.

ex.en: My mom kissed me on the cheek.

cards.note: Where takes the ablative: *yanağından öpmek* (to kiss on the cheek). *Öpüşmek* = to kiss each other. *Öptüm* closes a message to family or friends (Kisses).

ex.en: My family lives in the north of Turkey.

cards.note: *Kuzeyde* = in the north; *Kuzey Amerika* = North America. The others: *güney, doğu, batı*.

ex.en: I convinced her to come.

cards.note: What you persuade someone to do takes the dative: *gelmeye ikna etmek*. *İkna olmak* = to be convinced.

ex.en: There's a big hole in my sock.

cards.note: From *delmek* (to pierce). The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *deliği*. *Delikli* = with holes. Not *deli* (crazy).

ex.en: Could you correct my mistakes?

cards.note: From *düz* (straight, flat). *Düzelmek* = to get better, by itself: *Hava düzeldi* (The weather has cleared up).

ex.en: Are you married or single?

cards.note: *Ev* (home) + `-lI`. *Evlenmek* = to get married (to: *ile*); *evlilik* = marriage.

ex.en: Learning a foreign language isn't hard.

cards.note: As a noun, a foreigner or a stranger: *Yabancılarla konuşma* (Don't talk to strangers). *Yabancı dil* = foreign language.

en: to get on, to get in (a vehicle)

ex.en: We got on the wrong bus!

cards.note: The vehicle takes the dative: *otobüse binmek*, *ata binmek* (to ride a horse). The opposite is *inmek*, with the ablative.

ex.en: I share my room with my brother.

cards.note: With whom: *ile*. From *pay* (share, portion). Also on social media: *fotoğraf paylaşmak*.

ex.en: The kitchen smells wonderful.

cards.note: The thing gives off the smell: *Bu süt kokuyor* (This milk smells bad). To smell something yourself is *koklamak*; a smell is *koku*.

ex.en: Please take one step back.

cards.note: *Adım atmak* = to take a step. Not to be confused with *adım* = my name (*ad* + `-Im`), as in *Benim adım Ece*.

ex.en: I work freelance; I don't have an office.

cards.note: Free as in not held or not restricted: *Polis onu serbest bıraktı* (The police released him). Free of charge is *ücretsiz* or *bedava*; free time is *boş*.

ex.tr: Burada deniz çok derin, dikkat et.
ex.en: The sea is very deep here; be careful.

cards.note: *Derin bir nefes al* = Take a deep breath. *Derinlik* = depth; the opposite is *sığ* (shallow).

ex.en: For example, we could go to the movies tonight.

cards.note: Everyday; *örneğin* is more formal. *Mesela?* = Like what?

ex.en: Is breakfast included in the price?

cards.note: Spelled with â (TDK). After the dative, included in (*fiyata dâhil*); after the nominative, including (*ben dâhil herkes*, everyone including me). *Dâhil etmek* = to include.

ex.en: Class starts at eight in the morning.

cards.note: *Sekizinci* = eighth; *sekiz yüz* = eight hundred.

ex.en: Between you and me, I don't like him at all.

cards.note: Colloquial for *söz*. *Laf etmek* = to talk, to gossip; *Lafımı kesme!* = Don't interrupt me! *Laf aramızda* = between you and me.

ex.en: My dream has finally come true!

cards.note: From *gerçek* (real) + `-lAş`. Formal for events: *Toplantı yarın gerçekleşecek* (The meeting will take place tomorrow).

en: to hit, to crash into, to bump into

ex.en: The car crashed into a tree.

cards.note: What is hit takes the dative: *duvara çarpmak*. In arithmetic, to multiply: *İki çarpı üç altı eder* (Two times three is six). A heart *çarpar* when it races.

ex.tr: Bu ay üçüncü kez geç kaldın!
ex.en: That's the third time you've been late this month!

cards.note: *Üç* + `-(I)ncI`. *Üçüncü olmak* = to come third.

ex.en: The general gave the soldiers orders.

cards.note: Takes front-vowel suffixes, like *saat*: *generali*, *generaller*. Soldiers address an officer as *Komutanım*.

ex.en: I wrapped the present in nice paper.

cards.note: What you wrap it in takes the dative: *kâğıda sarmak*. Colloquially, to grab your interest: *Bu dizi beni sardı* (I'm hooked on this show). *Sarılmak* = to hug.

en: to fill out, to fill in (a form)

ex.en: Please fill out this form.

cards.note: Causative of *dolmak* (to become full). *Bardağı suyla doldurdu* = He filled the glass with water.

ex.en: Our teacher is very patient.

cards.note: From *öğretmek* (to teach). Pupils call their teacher *Öğretmenim* or *Hocam*.

ex.tr: Derdin ne? Neden bu kadar sessizsin?
ex.en: What's wrong? Why are you so quiet?

cards.note: The t becomes d before a vowel: *derdi*, *derdim*. *Dert etme* = Don't worry about it; *dertli* = troubled.

ex.en: There's still hope; don't give up.

cards.note: The t becomes d before a vowel: *umudu*, *umudum*. *Umut etmek* = to hope; *umarım* (from *ummak*) = I hope. Synonym: *ümit*.

en: to bring down, to lower (a price, a fever)

ex.en: I dropped my phone again.

cards.note: Causative of *düşmek* (to fall). *Ateşi düşürmek* = to bring a fever down; *fiyatı düşürmek* = to lower the price.

ex.en: I'm sleepy; I'm going to bed.

cards.note: From *uyumak* (to sleep). *Uykum var* or *Uykum geldi* = I'm sleepy; *uykusuz* = sleepless; *İyi uykular* = Sleep well.

ex.en: Can you prove it?

cards.note: From *kanıt* (proof, evidence) + `-lA`. The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *kanıtlıyor*. What is proved is often a noun clause: *haklı olduğunu kanıtlamak*.

ex.tr: Bir kadeh kırmızı şarap alabilir miyim?
ex.en: Could I have a glass of red wine?

cards.note: The p becomes b before a vowel: *şarabı*. *Beyaz şarap* = white wine; *kadeh* = wine glass.

ex.en: I have a surprise for you!

cards.note: *Sürpriz yapmak* = to surprise someone (dative); *sürpriz parti* = surprise party. To be surprised is *şaşırmak*.

ex.en: The colour of this dress is lovely.

cards.note: The k becomes g before a vowel: *rengi*. *Ne renk?* = What colour? *Renkli* = colourful.

ex.en: Will you have another tea?

cards.note: Served in small tulip-shaped glasses, often all day long. *Çaycı* = tea seller; *çay bahçesi* = tea garden. Another word *çay* means stream.

ex.en: You can't come? What a pity!

cards.note: *Yazık ona* = Poor thing; *Yazık oldu* = What a waste. Also a reproach: *Yazık sana!* (Shame on you!)

ex.en: Doctor, I have chest pain.

cards.note: The ü drops before a vowel: *göğsü*, *göğsüm*. *Göğüs ağrısı* = chest pain.

ex.en: The police examined the camera footage.

cards.note: From *ince* (thin, fine) + `-lA`: to look at closely. The e becomes i before `-(I)yor`: *inceliyor*. *İnceleme* = review, study.

ex.en: I'm a witness to this accident.

cards.note: From *tanımak* (to know). The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *tanığı*. *Tanıklık etmek* = to testify. Also *şahit*.

ex.tr: Köprünün ötesinde güzel bir kafe var.
ex.en: There's a nice café beyond the bridge.

cards.note: Used like a place noun: *denizin ötesinde* (beyond the sea). *Öte yandan* = on the other hand; *öteki* = the other one.

ex.en: There's still snow on top of the mountain.

cards.note: *Dağa çıkmak* = to climb a mountain; *dağlık* = mountainous. *Ağrı Dağı* = Mount Ararat.

ex.en: You need to rest a little.

cards.note: Also the passive of *dinlemek*: *Bu şarkı çok dinlendi* (This song was played a lot). *Dinlenme* = rest.

ex.en: Who's responsible for this?

cards.note: What you're responsible for takes the ablative: *Bundan ben sorumluyum*. *Sorumluluk* = responsibility. As a noun, the person in charge: *mağaza sorumlusu*.

ex.en: In summer we go south, to Antalya.

cards.note: *Güneyde* = in the south; *Güney Afrika* = South Africa. Not *güneş* (sun).

ex.en: My sister is pregnant; she's giving birth in August.

cards.note: *Gebe* is more formal or medical. *Hamile kalmak* = to get pregnant; *Kaç aylık hamile?* = How many months pregnant is she?

ex.en: My dad reads the paper every morning.

cards.note: *Gazeteci* = journalist; *gazete bayii* = newsstand.

ex.en: She came first in the competition.

cards.note: *Bir* + `-(I)ncI`. Also top quality: *birinci sınıf* (first-class). *İlk* is also first, and more common before a noun: *ilk gün* (the first day).

ex.en: Did you get into a fight with someone at school?

cards.note: Reciprocal of *dövmek* (to beat): to fight with fists, with someone: *ile*. A row, with words or fists, is a *kavga*.

ex.en: We grow tomatoes in the garden.

cards.note: *Çay bahçesi* = outdoor tea garden; *hayvanat bahçesi* = zoo; *bahçeli* = with a garden.

ex.tr: Sana bir tavsiyem var: erken yat.
ex.en: I have some advice for you: go to bed early.

cards.note: *Tavsiye etmek* = to recommend, to advise, to someone: dative. *Bu kitabı sana tavsiye ederim* = I recommend this book to you.

ex.en: Well done, you got all the questions right!

cards.note: Praise, usually to a child or someone younger; to a peer or someone older, *Tebrikler* or *Bravo* sound better. Said ironically, it stings.

en: to get angry, to be cross

ex.en: Please don't be angry with me; I didn't do it on purpose.

cards.note: Who or what you're angry at takes the dative: *bana kızma*. The adjective is *kızgın* (angry); *kızdırmak* = to make angry.

ex.en: How tall are you?

cards.note: *Uzun boylu* = tall, *kısa boylu* = short (of people); *boy boy* = in all sizes; *boyunca* = all along, throughout.

ex.tr: Bu filmde küçük bir rolü var.
ex.en: He has a small part in this movie.

cards.note: Takes front-vowel suffixes (TDK): *rolü*, *roller*. *Rol yapmak* = to put on an act; *rol oynamak* = to play a part.

en: to appear, to seem, to look
to be seen, to show up

ex.en: You look very tired today.

cards.note: Colloquial for *görünmek*: *mutlu gözüküyor* (he looks happy). Also to show up: *Bir daha buralarda gözükme!*

ex.en: My dad never bets.

cards.note: The i drops before a vowel: *bahsi*. *Bahse girerim* = I bet (also *iddiaya girerim*). In formal Turkish also a topic: *bahis konusu* (in question).

ex.en: Could you give me an example?

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *örneği*. *Örneğin* = for example (more formal than *mesela*); *örnek olmak* = to set an example.

ex.en: That's what they call fate.

cards.note: No vowel drop: *kaderim*. *Kaderin cilvesi* = a twist of fate. Also *alın yazısı*, literally what is written on the forehead.

ex.en: Exams are over; we're free now!

cards.note: Free as in not captive or not controlled: *özgür bir ülke*. Free of charge is *ücretsiz* or *bedava*. *Özgürlük* = freedom. Synonym: *hür*.

ex.en: My dad works at a public hospital.

cards.note: *Devlet* is the state; the government in power is the *hükümet*. *Devlet okulu* = public school; *devlet memuru* = civil servant.

ex.tr: Televizyonda görüntü yok, sadece ses var.
ex.en: There's no picture on the TV, only sound.

cards.note: From *görmek* (to see). *Görüntülü arama* = video call.

ex.en: She won two awards this year.

cards.note: *Ödül almak* or *kazanmak* = to win an award; *ödül töreni* = awards ceremony; *ödüllü* = award-winning.

ex.en: She politely turned down my offer.

cards.note: *Ret* (refusal) + *etmek*, written as one word with a double d. What you refuse takes the accusative: *teklifi reddetmek*.

ex.en: The sky is very blue today.

cards.note: Like the other colour words, a noun and an adjective. *Açık mavi* = light blue; *lacivert* = navy blue.

ex.en: Where are you going on vacation this summer?

cards.note: *Tatile gitmek* = to go on vacation; *tatil yapmak* = to take a holiday; *resmî tatil* = public holiday.

ex.en: At the wedding, the party went on until morning.

cards.note: From *eğlenmek* (to have fun). *Eğlenceli* = fun, entertaining; *İyi eğlenceler!* = Have fun!

ex.en: The children go to school on the school bus.

cards.note: In Turkey a *servis* is also the minibus that takes pupils to school or staff to work. In a restaurant: *Servis çok yavaştı* (The service was very slow).

ex.en: I have no energy at all today.

cards.note: *Enerji içeceği* = energy drink; *güneş enerjisi* = solar energy; *enerjik* = energetic.

ex.tr: Yeni işim için iki haftalık eğitim alıyorum.
ex.en: I'm getting two weeks of training for my new job.

cards.note: From *eğitmek* (to educate, to train). *Eğitim almak* = to get training; *eğitimli* = educated; *uzaktan eğitim* = distance learning.

ex.en: Why are you so angry with me?

cards.note: Angry with someone: dative, *bana kızgın*. From *kızmak* (to get angry). Also very hot: *kızgın yağ* (sizzling oil).

ex.en: This takes courage.

cards.note: *Cesaretli* = brave; *cesaret etmek* = to dare (dative): *Konuşmaya cesaret edemedim* (I didn't dare speak).

ex.en: Has the cut on your knee healed?

cards.note: *Yaralı* = injured; *yaralamak* = to injure; *yara bandı* = adhesive bandage; *yara izi* = scar.

ex.en: I bought two tickets for the concert.

cards.note: *Gidiş dönüş bilet* = round-trip ticket; *gişe* = ticket office, box office.

ex.en: Can you text me your address?

cards.note: *Ev adresi* = home address; *e-posta adresi* = email address. *Adres tarifi* = directions to a place.

ex.en: Ms Ayşe is waiting for you.

cards.note: After a first name it is capitalized: *Ayşe Hanım*. *Hanımlar* = ladies; colloquially *bizim hanım* = my wife. *Hanımefendi* = madam.

ex.tr: Sonunda yeni bir araba satın aldık.
ex.en: We finally bought a new car.

cards.note: More formal than plain *almak*, and clearer when *almak* could mean to take. *Satın alma* = purchasing.

ex.en: What kind of music do you like?

cards.note: Colloquially a person, often with a judgment: *Garip bir tip* (A strange character); *Tipine bak!* (Look at him!). Not *tıp* (medicine).

ex.en: The guests are sitting in the living room.

cards.note: In a Turkish home the *salon* is the main room, where guests sit. Also a hall: *düğün salonu* (wedding hall), *spor salonu* (gym), *kuaför salonu* (hair salon).

ex.tr: Sizden bir şey rica edebilir miyim?
ex.en: May I ask you a favour?

cards.note: The person asked takes the ablative: *Sizden bir ricam var* (I have a favour to ask you). *Rica ederim* = You're welcome, the reply to *teşekkür ederim*.

ex.en: Do you believe in ghosts?

cards.note: From *hayal* (image, dream). *Hayalet gibi* = like a ghost (pale, silent). In folk tales also *hortlak*.

ex.en: This bag is fake, not the original.

cards.note: *Sahte pasaport* = false passport; *sahte bir gülümseme* = a fake smile. A fake designer item is also *çakma* (colloquial).

ex.tr: Bu dükkânda yüz çeşit peynir var.
ex.en: This shop has a hundred kinds of cheese.

cards.note: The t becomes d before a vowel: *çeşidi*. *Her çeşit* = all kinds of; *çeşitli* = various; *çeşit çeşit* = all sorts of.

ex.en: That's a very sensible idea.

cards.note: *Mantık* (logic) + `-lI`. *Mantıksız* = illogical, unreasonable. *Mantıklı ol!* = Be reasonable!

ex.en: It's extremely hot today.

cards.note: Also an adjective: *aşırı hız* (excessive speed). In young people's speech, a strong intensifier: *aşırı güzel* (really nice).

ex.en: Last night I beat my dad at chess.

cards.note: Who you beat takes the accusative: *rakibi yenmek*. A homonym is the passive of *yemek*: *Bu mantar yenmez* (This mushroom isn't edible). *Yenilmek* = to be beaten.

ex.en: Health is more important than anything.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *sağlığı*. *Sağlıklı* = healthy; *Sağlık olsun* = Never mind (after a loss); *Elinize sağlık* = Thank you (to a cook).

ex.en: Could you put some ice in my drink?

cards.note: *Buz gibi* = ice-cold: *buz gibi bir su*. *Buzdolabı* = fridge; *buz pateni* = ice skating.

ex.tr: Bilim insanları yeni bir gezegen buldu.
ex.en: Scientists have found a new planet.

cards.note: From *bilmek* (to know). *Bilim insanı* (or *bilim adamı*) = scientist; *bilimsel* = scientific; *bilim kurgu* = science fiction.

ex.en: The trip takes about two hours.

cards.note: From *yaklaşmak* (to approach). Also *aşağı yukarı* (roughly), or *kadar* after the number: *iki saat kadar*.

ex.en: The captain will be here shortly.

cards.note: Literally head of a hundred. The captain of a ship, a plane or a team is a *kaptan*.

ex.en: The tip of the pencil broke.

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *ucu*, though most one-syllable words keep their consonant. Not *uç!*, the imperative of *uçmak* (to fly).

ex.en: The government announced a new decision.

cards.note: The government in power; the state is the *devlet*. *Hükümet binası* = government building.

ex.en: Why did you get up so early?

cards.note: *Ne* + *için*, literally what for. A little formal: *neden* is neutral, *niye* casual.

en: to be embarrassed, to be ashamed

ex.en: I was so embarrassed; everyone looked at me.

cards.note: What you're ashamed of takes the ablative: *Yaptığımdan utanıyorum*. *Utangaç* = shy; *Utanmıyor musun?* = Aren't you ashamed?

ex.en: This document is required for the application.

cards.note: *Gerek* (need) + `-lI`. *Gereksiz* = unnecessary; *gerekirse* = if necessary.

ex.en: My back really hurts.

cards.note: *Sırt çantası* = backpack; *sırtüstü* = on your back. The lower back is *bel*.

ex.en: Thank goodness, everyone's fine.

cards.note: Mostly in set phrases: *Çok şükür* (Thank goodness; also in answer to *Nasılsın?*), *Allah'a şükür*. The ü drops before a vowel: *şükrü*. *Şükretmek* = to give thanks.

ex.tr: Çiftlikte domuz yok, sadece inek ve koyun var.
ex.en: There are no pigs on the farm, only cows and sheep.

cards.note: *Domuz eti* = pork, rarely eaten in Turkey; *yaban domuzu* = wild boar. Also an insult.

ex.en: Is there anything else you'd like?

cards.note: From *istemek* (to want). The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *isteği*. *İsteyerek* = willingly; *isteksiz* = reluctant.

ex.en: My mom is a famous stage actress.

cards.note: *Oyun* (game, play) + `-CI`: one word for an actor and a player. *Futbolcu* = soccer player.

ex.en: Banks are closed on Sunday.

cards.note: Opposite of *açık*. *Hava kapalı* = It's overcast; *Telefonum kapalıydı* = My phone was off.

ex.en: What's this tool for?

cards.note: *Alet çantası* = toolbox; *müzik aleti* = musical instrument; *elektrikli aletler* = electrical appliances.

ex.en: Please sign here.

cards.note: From *imza* (signature) + `-lA`. The a becomes ı before `-(I)yor`: *imzalıyor*. Also *imza atmak* (to sign).

ex.en: From this point of view, you're right.

cards.note: An angle in geometry and in photos (*güzel bir açı*); *bu açıdan* = from this angle, in this respect. Not *acı* (pain; bitter).

ex.en: The judge will announce the decision tomorrow.

cards.note: The ç becomes c before a vowel: *yargıcı*. Turkish courts officially say *hâkim*; *yargıç* is its Turkish synonym, frequent in dubbed films.

ex.en: Quite the opposite, I'm very pleased!

cards.note: As an adjective: *ters yön* (the wrong way); *Ters giden bir şey var* (Something is going wrong). *Tersine* = on the contrary.

ex.en: This knife doesn't cut at all.

cards.note: The k becomes ğ before a vowel: *bıçağı*. *Ekmek bıçağı* = bread knife; *çatal bıçak* = cutlery.

ex.tr: Ne önerirsin, balık mı, et mi?
ex.en: What do you suggest, fish or meat?

cards.note: To someone: dative, *sana bir şey önereceğim*. *Öneri* = suggestion. Close to *tavsiye etmek* (to recommend).

en: to make it (in time), to catch (dative)

ex.en: We caught the train at the last minute.

cards.note: What you make it to takes the dative: *toplantıya yetişmek*. Also to grow up (*İzmir'de yetiştim*) and, of plants, to grow. *Yetiştirmek* = to grow, to raise.

ex.en: The rain ruined all our plans.

cards.note: *Bozulmak* = to break down, to go bad: *Araba bozuldu*. *Para bozmak* = to break a bill; *bozuk para* = coins, change.

en: to fit in, to take a place

ex.en: Have you settled into the new house?

cards.note: From *yer* (place) + `-lAş`. Where takes the dative: *İstanbul'a yerleşmek* (to settle in Istanbul). *Yerleştirmek* = to put in place, to put away.

ex.en: I'm under a lot of pressure at work.

cards.note: From *basmak* (to press, to print). *Baskı altında* = under pressure; *ikinci baskı* = second printing (of a book).

ex.en: The king and queen came out onto the balcony.

cards.note: From *kral* (king). In chess the queen is the *vezir*. *Güzellik kraliçesi* = beauty queen.

ex.en: Could you open the window? It's very hot.

cards.note: *Pencere kenarı* = window seat (on a plane or a bus); *pencereden bakmak* = to look out of the window.

ex.en: The pharmacy is on the corner, next to the bank.

cards.note: *Köşede* = on the corner; *köşeyi dönmek* = to turn the corner, and colloquially to strike it rich. *Köşe yazarı* = columnist.

ex.en: This noise is getting on my nerves.

cards.note: *Sinirli* = irritable, angry; *sinirlenmek* = to get annoyed; *Sinirim bozuldu* = I got really annoyed.

ex.en: How are you doing, buddy?

cards.note: Mostly in dubbed films, for English **buddy** or **dude**; friends in real life say *kanka* or *dostum*. Its older sense is an acquaintance. The p becomes b before a vowel: *ahbabı*.

ex.tr: Otobüs her yirmi dakikada bir geliyor.
ex.en: The bus comes every twenty minutes.

cards.note: *Otobüs durağı* = bus stop. Intercity buses leave from the *otogar*.

ex.en: My sister studies art at university.

cards.note: *Sanatçı* = artist; *sanat eseri* = work of art; *güzel sanatlar* = fine arts; *el sanatları* = handicrafts.
